mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the average return is not statistically below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above their 12-month moving averages signals robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 0.1 percentage points for six consecutive months despite steady GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates labor market softness without economic contraction, which typically precedes a mild equity pullback, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises < 0.1pp for 6 consecutive months AND GDPC1 > 0% YoY
regime_hint: labor market softness with economic growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month average for five consecutive months signals strengthening residential demand, which boosts construction and related sector earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.
